name: Battle of Isandlwana
note: The accounts do not say where the Zulu stood or in which direction they came, so they are placed at the top of the plan and the British camp at the foot; the hill of Isandlwana is placed on the British left, as the accounts put the Zulu movement round it, but its exact position is not given. The donga is placed on the British right flank as stated. The accounts say the valley where the Zulu waited may have been the Ngwebeni or closer, so no valley is drawn. The Zulu reserve is shown unengaged; the accounts give no position for it. Other accounts give different details of the last stands.

terrain.name: Isandlwana
terrain.quote: moving to the British left around the hill of Isandlwana

terrain.name: Donga
terrain.quote: retreated to a donga, a dried-out watercourse, on the British right flank

units.name: Zulu right horn
units.quote: uDududu, uNokenke regiments, part uNodwengu corps

units.name: Zulu chest
units.quote: umCijo, uKhandampevu, regiments; part uNodwengu corps

units.name: Zulu left horn
units.quote: the left horn of the Zulu advance was moving to outflank and envelop

units.name: Zulu reserve (the loins)
units.quote: Undi corps, uDloko, iNdluyengwe, Indlondlo and Uthulwana regiments

units.name: British camp
units.quote: The British under Chelmsford pitched camp at Isandlwana on 20 January

units.name: Companies of the 24th Foot
units.quote: all six companies of the 24th Foot into an extended firing line

units.name: Two 7-pounder guns
units.quote: two 7-pounder guns with around 70 men of the Royal Artillery

units.name: Durnford's column
units.quote: arrived from Rorke's Drift with 500 men of the Natal Native Contingent

units.name: Rocket battery
units.quote: a rocket battery of two 9pr Hale rocket troughs of the No. 2 Column

units.name: G Company, 2nd/24th
units.quote: exposed the flank of G Company, 2nd/24th

phases.title: The Zulu army is found near the camp
phases.text: Scouts chased some Zulus into a valley and saw most of the main force sitting in total quiet. Durnford had reached the camp with his men and a rocket battery, and Pulleine held the camp with the 24th and two guns.
phases.quote: most of the 20,000 men of the main enemy force sitting in total quiet

phases.title: The Zulu advance and the British extend their line
phases.text: Having been discovered, the Zulu leapt to the offensive in the horns and chest of the buffalo. Pulleine sent all six companies of the 24th out into an extended firing line, and Durnford's men moved forward.
phases.quote: Pulleine sent out first one, then all six companies of the 24th Foot into an extended firing line

phases.title: Durnford falls back to a donga
phases.text: Durnford's men met part of the Zulu centre, retreated to a donga on the British right flank and formed a defensive line there. The rocket battery fell behind, fired three rockets and was overrun.
phases.quote: Durnford's men, upon meeting elements of the Zulu centre, had retreated to a donga

phases.title: Pulleine draws the firing line closer to the camp
phases.text: After about twenty minutes of firing, Pulleine made his one change to the original dispositions. He brought the companies in the firing line slightly closer to the camp.
phases.quote: Pulleine only made one change to the original disposition after about 20 minutes of firing, bringing in the companies in the firing line slightly closer to the camp.

phases.title: Volleys pin the centre while the left horn swings out
phases.text: For an hour or so the British volleys and the artillery held the Zulu centre. Meanwhile the left horn moved to outflank and envelop the British right.
phases.quote: the left horn of the Zulu advance was moving to outflank and envelop the British right

phases.title: Durnford's men withdraw and G Company is overrun
phases.text: Durnford's men, who had fought the longest, began to withdraw and their rate of fire fell. Their retreat exposed the flank of G Company, which the Zulu left horn overran relatively quickly.
phases.quote: Durnford's retreat, however, exposed the flank of G Company, 2nd/24th, which was overrun relatively quickly.

phases.title: The 24th falls back to the camp
phases.text: Durnford's withdrawal exposed the right flank of the regulars and the Zulu threatened to encircle them, so Pulleine ordered a withdrawal to the camp. The men of the 24th fell back fighting, in order and with discipline.
phases.quote: The regulars' retreat was performed with order and discipline and the men of the 24th conducted a fighting withdrawal into the camp.

phases.title: The Zulu close in on the camp
phases.text: The Zulu pressed into the camp and fought hand to hand. Evidence shows large groups of bodies around the camp, and the slaughter was complete in the area around it.
phases.quote: the slaughter was complete in the area around the camp
